items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says the 'left boundary is clamped' but writes Γ_D = {0}×(−0.5,0.5). In Ω = (−1,1)×(−0.5,0.5) the left edge is x = −1; x = 0 is the vertical mid-line inside the domain. The 3D cantilever ({−1}×…) and eigenvalue case (g) both use x = −1. Clamping the mid-line literally would cut off the left half from the load. Because β|Ω| = 1 equals the area of the right half, the optimum would then be a trivially solid right half, which contradicts the truss-like design the paper reports. Fig. 4 would settle this but is not available.
readings: Clamp the full left edge x = −1, y ∈ [−0.5, 0.5] (treat {0} as a typo for {−1})
Clamp the vertical line x = 0, y ∈ [−0.5, 0.5] exactly as written (the left half x < 0 carries no load)

items.entity: Downward load on the right edge
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 calls it a 'point load' at the centre of the right boundary but defines it as a traction t on the segment Γ_N = {1}×(−0.05,0.05), 10% of the edge height. The traction is integrated as ∫_ΓN t·u ds using 500 points on the 'non-homogeneous Neumann boundary' (Sec. 4.1.4). The text does not settle whether this is a concentrated nodal force or a uniformly distributed patch load.
readings: Concentrated nodal force at (x, y) = (1, 0)
Uniform traction on x = 1, y ∈ [−0.05, 0.05] (about 6 element edges on a 120×60 grid, 10 on 200×100)

items.entity: Downward load on the right edge (total force)
items.description: t = (0,−1)ᵀ is called a 'point load', which would mean a total force of 1. But it is used as a traction density on a segment 0.1 long, which gives a total force of 0.1. Table 3 reports compliance 0.5953 (APF-FNN) and 0.6930 (FEM-PF) for case (a). That is about what a total force of 0.1 with E = 1 gives; a unit force would give roughly 100× more (order 60). Compliance scales with F², so the two readings differ by a factor of 100. Caveat: if the paper's absolute-weight Ginzburg–Landau term (γ = 0.01) and volume penalty are copied, the load scale also changes how strongly they weigh against compliance.
readings: Total downward force 0.1 (traction 1 per unit length over the 0.1-long segment)
Total downward force 1 (unit point load, or traction 10 over the segment)

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs. plane strain) and thickness
items.description: Sec. 3.2.1 writes C0 using the 3D Lamé constant λ = Eν/((1+ν)(1−2ν)); applied to a 2D field this is plane strain. The paper never says plane stress or plane strain, and never gives an out-of-plane thickness. Grid-based SIMP codes usually default to plane stress with unit thickness. Plane strain equals plane stress with E/(1−ν²) and an effective ν of 0.3/0.7 ≈ 0.43, so switching is not just a rescaling.
readings: Plane strain, E = 1, ν = 0.3, unit depth (the given λ, μ used literally)
Plane stress, E = 1, ν = 0.3, unit thickness

items.entity: Grid resolution and element type for design and analysis
items.description: APF-FNN uses no mesh. It uses 2×10⁴ interior points on a regular grid (200×100 according to the sampling study in Sec. 4.1.4) plus 500 boundary points. The only grid-based run is the FEM-PF baseline on a '120×60 mesh' in FEniCS (Sec. 4.1.3); element type and order (quads or triangles) are not stated. No grid is named as the problem's own discretization. Because ε = 0.01 is fixed, the result depends on element size: on 120×60, ε is smaller than h = 1/60.
readings: 120×60 elements, h = 1/60 (FEM-PF baseline)
200×100 elements, h = 0.01 (matches the APF-FNN interior point grid)

items.description: The paper uses no density or sensitivity filter. Its length scale comes from two places: the Ginzburg–Landau term with ε = γ = 0.01, given in absolute units and not normalized by compliance; and the limited frequency range of the topology network (12×12 Fourier modes, ω_max^φ). No equivalent filter type or radius is given for a grid-based SIMP solver.
readings: No filter; add the term γ∫(ε/2|∇φ|² + φ²(1−φ)²/(4ε))dx with ε = γ = 0.01 to the objective, as the paper and FEM-PF do
Standard density filter with radius about 1.5 elements (≈0.025 on 120×60, ≈0.015 on 200×100)
Larger density or sensitivity filter radius (≈0.05–0.1) to mimic the smooth output of the topology network

items.entity: Topology-network Fourier bandwidth ω_max^φ (sets the finest design feature)
items.description: Table 2 and Sec. 4.1.2 give ω_max^u = 35 and ω_max^φ = 30 for case (a). Sec. 4.1.4 gives the reference setting for case (a) as ω_max^φ = 35 and ω_max^u = 30, i.e. swapped. The Fig. 13 caption is also garbled. Fig. 13 shows that ω_max^φ controls how much fine detail the design has, so it acts as a hidden length scale.
readings: ω_max^φ = 30 (state ω_max^u = 35), from Table 2 and Sec. 4.1.2
ω_max^φ = 35 (state ω_max^u = 30), from Sec. 4.1.4

items.description: β = 0.5 is imposed only through the quadratic penalty λ_penal(∫φ − β|Ω|)². The starting value is given only as 'O(1)' and is not listed in Table 2. It is divided by ζ = 0.98 after every outer iteration, growing to 'O(10³–10⁴)' (Sec. 4.1.2, Alg. 1). So the final volume is not exactly 0.5, and how the penalty is ramped may affect which design is reached. A grid solver with a hard volume constraint behaves differently.
readings: Hard constraint ∫φ = 0.5|Ω| (OC or MMA)
Penalty starting at λ⁽⁰⁾ = 1, divided by 0.98 every iteration (≈2.4×10⁴ after 500)
Penalty starting at λ⁽⁰⁾ = 0.1, divided by 0.98 every iteration (≈2.4×10³ after 500)

items.entity: Optimizer and iteration budget for a grid-based run
items.description: The grid-based reference is FEM-PF (Sec. 4.1.3): an L² gradient flow using the semi-implicit scheme of ref. [21], 100 outer × 20 inner iterations. Its pseudo-time step, penalty updates and stopping rule are not given. APF-FNN instead uses Adam for 500 outer iterations. The two methods reach different designs (compliance differs by 14%, Fig. 8), so the update scheme affects the result.
readings: Copy FEM-PF: Allen–Cahn L² gradient flow, 100 outer × 20 inner steps, pseudo-time step chosen by the user
Standard SIMP update (OC or MMA) for 500 iterations or until converged
